item.title: Q&A: 'We need an agency to bring cutting-edge global expertise to Sweden'
item.description: Sweden's Labour Minister Johan Britz, who represents the Liberal Party, recently called for a new government agency to be launched in Sweden that will take over responsibility for work permits from the Migration Agency. He explains why.

item.title: 'Betrayed': How layoffs at Ericsson's Swedish offices are affecting our readers
item.description: In a recent survey we asked readers working at Ericsson how the recent news of yet another round of layoffs ‒ the third in as many years ‒ is affecting them. Here's what they said.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: varuberg
item.description: Understanding this peculiar word will help you to avoid accidentally alienating people in Sweden.

item.title: Sweden's government asks Migration Agency to propose exemptions to work permit law
item.description: Sweden's government has ordered the Migration Agency to draw up a list of in demand professions which will be exempted from the new higher salary requirement set to come into force later this year.

item.title: OPINION: Are tips in Sweden becoming the norm?
item.description: Should you tip in Sweden? Habits are changing fast thanks to new technology and a hard-pressed restaurant trade, writes James Savage.

item.title: How you can get your Swedish employer to pay for your gym membership
item.description: Set yourself the New Year's resolution of getting fit this year? Many Swedish companies offer their employees 'friskvårdsbidrag', a tax-free lump sum for "activities which incorporate some form of exercise" (like a gym membership) or "de-stressing" activities, such as a massage.

item.title: How important is US trade and will Sweden join the euro?
item.description: In this week's podcast: how dependent is Sweden's economy on the US? New words in the Swedish dictionary, Migration Agency rejects high school exchange students, and a clampdown on abuse of student visas.

item.title: EU delays full rollout of EES border system over travel chaos concerns
item.description: The deadline for the full implementation of the Europe's Entry/Exit System (EES), the new EU digital border system, has been postponed from April to September amid concerns over travel disruptions during the summer season, a European Commission spokesperson said on Friday.

item.title: Olympics, pensions and sportlov: What changes in Sweden in February 2026
item.description: Will Sweden bring back gold at the Winter Olympics? Will the Melodifestivalen music contest throw up any half decent songs? Here are some of the main things happening in Sweden in February.

item.title: Inside Sweden: Do Swedish parent-teacher meetings have to be quite so unproductive?
item.description: Nordic Editor Richard Orange moans about parent-teacher meetings in Sweden before running through the stories The Local has covered this week, from work permit exemptions to euro membership and Ericsson layoffs.
